speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing the double vision, and does it get worse as the day goes on? Also, has anyone noticed drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did these symptoms, particularly the clumsiness and unsteady gait, appear suddenly or develop gradually over days or weeks? Also, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or loss of sensation in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent use of natalizumab, have you noticed any new headaches, fever, or changes in your mental status? I also need to know if your double vision and weakness have progressed rapidly over the last few weeks.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent natalizumab use and the combination of ataxia, weakness, and double vision, I suspect an opportunistic infection. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST TEST: JC Virus DNA in CSF.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The requested tests (MRI Brain with contrast and JC Virus DNA in CSF) were not performed or their results are not included in the provided data. Available readings: Vital signs are stable (Temp 36.6°C, BP 125/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min). Neurological exam shows right upper eyelid ptosis worsening with sustained upward gaze, diminished motor strength in upper extremities, but normal reflexes and sensation. Blood tests show elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies. Electromyography reveals decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation. Chest CT is normal with no thymoma detected.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies and the pattern of worsening ptosis with fatigue confirm a diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis, likely unmasked or exacerbated by your recent natalizumab use.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
